# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

At Grey Shutters, October was a lovely month, as the hollow's birches changed to a shade as golden as sunshine, the maples past the orchard became a magnificent crimson, the wild cherry-trees lining the lane took on the most charming hues of dark red and bronzy green, and the fields basked in aftermaths.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0000 }

The environment's vibrant hues brought great delight to Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0001 }

“Oh, Thirza,” she cried out a certain Saturday morning, waltzing inside as her arms overflowed with stunning branches, “I’m thrilled that I inhabit a world containing Octobers. Wouldn't it be dreadful if we leaped straight from September into November? Observe these maple boughs. Do they not impart a thrill to you—a series of thrills? I intend to adorn my room using them.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0002 }

“Untidy objects,” uttered Thirza, a person without a particularly refined appreciation of beauty. “You pack your chamber altogether excessively with outside items, Nell. Sleeping quarters exist for rest.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0003 }

“Oh, and also envision, Thirza. And you are aware that a person can envision far better within a space that holds beautiful objects. These boughs will be placed by me inside the old blue jug and positioned upon my table.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0004 }

“Be careful not to spill leaves throughout the staircase, in that case. I am attending a gathering of the Aid Society in Delford during this afternoon, Nell, and it is unlikely I will return prior to dusk. Preparing supper for Obed and Tobias will fall to you, so see to it that you do not neglect setting the tea to steep until you are seated at the table like you were on the previous occasion.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0005 }

“My forgetting was terrible,” Nell admitted with regret, “however, I was attempting to devise a name for Primrose Dell that very afternoon, which pushed different matters from my mind. Obed behaved wonderfully. Not once did he reprimand me. Placing the tea down on his own, he remarked that we might just as easily delay for a time. Furthermore, I recounted a delightful fairy tale to him during our wait, which kept the duration from seeming lengthy to him. Thirza, that fairy tale was magnificent. Because its conclusion slipped my memory, I created a new ending on my own, and Obed mentioned that he was unable to discern the location of the seam.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0006 }

“Obed would find it completely fine, Nell, should you decide to rise and eat dinner at midnight. However, you must stay sharp this time. Also—I am uncertain whether I am acting correctly—it might render you even more confused—nevertheless, you are permitted to invite Isolde to come over, pass the afternoon together, and drink tea here.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0007 }

“Oh, Thirza!” Nell pressed her hands together. “How completely wonderful! You do possess an imagination after all, otherwise you would not have realized how much I have wanted that exact thing. It is going to feel so delightful and mature. I will certainly not forget to let the tea steep when guests are visiting. Oh, Thirza, am I allowed to utilize the rosebud spray tea set?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0008 }

“Certainly not! The tea set with the rosebuds! What will you think of next? You are aware that I only serve with it for the minister or the Aids. The old brown tea set is what you will lay out. However, unseal the small yellow crock containing cherry preserves. That ought to be consumed soon regardless—I think fermentation is starting. Additionally, slice a portion of fruit cake and set out a few cookies and snaps.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0009 }

“I can just picture myself at the head of the table, pouring out the tea,” said Nell, closing her eyes with delight. “And inquiring of Isolde whether she takes sugar! Though I know she doesn’t, I will naturally ask her as if I were unaware. And then urging her to have another slice of fruit cake and an additional serving of preserves. Oh, Thirza, merely thinking about it gives me a wonderful feeling. May I show her to the spare room to take off her hat upon her arrival? And afterwards into the parlor to be seated?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0010 }

“No. You and your guest may use the sitting room. However, a partially filled bottle of raspberry cordial remains from the recent church social. You can locate it on the second shelf inside the sitting-room closet, and you and Isolde are welcome to drink it, as well as have a cooky with it later in the afternoon, because I suspect Obed will arrive late for tea as a result of hauling potatoes to the vessel.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0011 }

Nell sped down toward the hollow, going by the Nymph’s Well and climbing the spruce trail up to Pear Hill, so she could invite Isolde for tea. Consequently, shortly after Thirza had taken the carriage to Delford, Isolde arrived, wearing her second-best dress and appearing precisely as one should when invited to tea. On ordinary occasions she would rush into the kitchen without a knock; yet on this occasion she tapped demurely on the front door. Furthermore, when Nell, clad in her own second best, demurely answered, each little girl shook hands with as much seriousness as though they were complete strangers. This artificial gravity persisted until Isolde had been brought to the east gable to remove her hat and subsequently remained seated for ten minutes inside the sitting room, her toes properly positioned.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0012 }

“In what state of health is your mother?” Nell asked with politeness, precisely as though she had not observed Mrs. Pembroke gathering apples during that same morning while in great spirits and vigor.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0013 }

“She is doing fine, thank you. Am I right in thinking Mr. Abernethy is carting potatoes over to the lily sands later today?” inquired Isolde, who had travelled down to Mr. Gorham Pullen’s earlier that morning aboard Obed’s cart.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0014 }

“Indeed. The yield from our potatoes is exceptionally high during this year. My hope is that the yield from your father’s crop is also high.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0015 }

“Thank you, it is quite good. Have you gathered a lot of your apples so far?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0016 }

“Oh, ever so many,” Nell said, abandoning her dignified composure as she leapt to her feet rapidly. “Isolde, let us head out to the orchard to gather some Red Sweetings. Thirza tells us that whatever remains on the tree is ours to take. Thirza possesses a very generous nature. She informed us that fruit cake and cherry preserves are available for tea. However, informing your guest about the food you plan to serve them breaches good manners, which means I will refrain from mentioning the beverage she stated we could enjoy. I will merely reveal that its name starts with an R and a C, plus its hue is bright red. Bright red beverages are a favorite of mine, aren't they yours? Their flavor surpasses drinks of any other shade by double.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0017 }

Because of its large, drooping branches that bowed to the earth under the weight of fruit, the orchard was so enchanting that the young girls remained there for the majority of the afternoon, resting in a patch of grass where the green grass had survived the frost and the mild fall sunlight stayed warm, consuming apples and conversing as fast as possible. Isolde possessed many details to relate to Nell regarding school events. She was forced to share a seat with Tibby Tulk and despised it; Tibby continually scraped her pencil, which caused her—Isolde's—blood to curdle; Opal Pettigrew had cured every single one of her warts, as sure as you're alive, utilizing an enchanted stone provided by old Mary Joe from the Creek. One was required to stroke the warts using the stone and subsequently toss it over one's left shoulder during the new moon, causing the warts to disappear entirely. Wilfred Mott's name appeared alongside Em White's on the porch wall, making Em White extremely angry; Sam Gammon had been disrespectful to Mr. Pidgeon during a lesson, prompting Mr. Pidgeon to cane him, which led Sam's father to visit the school and challenge Mr. Pidgeon to touch another of his offspring ever again; Mattie Pullen possessed a fresh red hood along with a tasseled blue crossover, acting so grandly because of them that it was utterly disgusting; Lizzie Duckett refused to talk to Mamie Wilson since Mamie Wilson's adult sister had stolen the boyfriend of Lizzie Duckett's adult sister; everyone felt Nell's absence intensely and desired her return to school; and Hugh Carrow—
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0018 }

However, Nell had no desire to listen to anything regarding Hugh Carrow. Springing to her feet with speed, she suggested that they ought to head inside to drink some raspberry cordial.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0019 }

Nell inspected the pantry’s second shelf in the room, yet the bottle of raspberry cordial was absent. Upon further searching, she discovered it tucked far behind on the highest shelf. Nell transferred it onto a tray, placing it alongside a tumbler on the table.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0020 }

“Isolde, do take some now, if you would,” she offered courteously. “I doubt I will partake at the moment. Having eaten all those apples, I simply lack the desire for anything else.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0021 }

After pouring a tumblerful for herself, Isolde admiringly observed its bright-red hue, and she subsequently sipped it with delicacy.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0022 }

“Nell, that raspberry cordial is remarkably good,” she remarked. “I was unaware that raspberry cordial tasted so wonderful.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0023 }

“I’m truly happy it pleases you. Have all that you desire. I will step outside for a moment to poke the fire. A great number of duties weigh upon one's thoughts when managing a home, don't they?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0024 }

By the time Nell returned from the kitchen, Isolde was consuming a second glass of cordial, and upon being urged by Nell, she raised no real opposition to consuming a third. These glasses were filled generously, and the raspberry cordial was undoubtedly quite delicious.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0025 }

“It’s the most delicious I’ve ever tasted,” Isolde remarked. “It is far better than the one Mrs. Sowerby makes, despite how much she boasts about her own. The flavor is completely different from hers.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0026 }

“I would imagine that the raspberry cordial made by Thirza would likely be far superior to Mrs. Sowerby’s,” Nell stated loyally. “Thirza has a great reputation as a cook. She attempts to instruct me in cooking, but I assure you, Isolde, the progress is very difficult. Cookery offers hardly any room for imagination. A person must simply follow instructions. When I last baked a cake, I neglected to add the flour. My mind was occupied with the most wonderful story concerning you and me, Isolde. In my mind, you were gravely sick with smallpox and abandoned by everyone, yet I fearlessly approached your bed and tended you until you recovered; subsequently, I contracted smallpox and perished, being interred beneath those poplar trees located in the cemetery, whereupon you set a rosebush near my grave and moistened it using your tears; furthermore, you never, ever erased the memory of the childhood friend who gave up her life on your behalf. Oh, Isolde, that story was so deeply touching. Tears poured continuously down my face as I stirred the cake ingredients. However, I omitted the flour, causing the cake to turn out as a complete disaster. You realize how indispensable flour is for baking cakes. Thirza felt extremely angry, and I cannot blame her. I cause her immense trouble. The incident with the pudding sauce last week humiliated her terribly. On Tuesday, we ate plum pudding for dinner, leaving half of the pudding along with a full pitcher of sauce behind. Thirza remarked that it would suffice for a second meal, directing me to place it upon the pantry shelf and place a cover over it. My intention was to cover it as completely as possible, Isolde, yet as I brought it inside, I pretended I was a nun—naturally, I am a Protestant, but I envisioned myself as a Catholic—taking vows to hide a broken heart inside a quiet convent; consequently, the necessity of covering the pudding sauce slipped my mind entirely. It occurred to me the following morning, prompting me to hurry to the pantry. Isolde, picture if you are able the sheer dread I felt upon discovering that a mouse had drowned inside that pudding sauce! Utilizing a spoon, I removed the mouse and tossed it outside into the yard, after which I rinsed the spoon using three separate bowls of water. Because Thirza was outside milking, I fully purposed to inquire of her upon her return whether I should feed the sauce to the pigs; nevertheless, upon her entry, I was pretending to be a frost fairy traveling through the forest to alter the colors of the trees to red and yellow according to their preferences, which caused me to completely forget the pudding sauce once more, and Thirza ordered me outdoors to gather apples. As it happened, Mr. and Mrs. Chester Ross hailing from Tullyvale arrived here during that morning. You are aware of how fashionable they are, particularly Mrs. Chester Ross. By the time Thirza summoned me inside, dinner was completely prepared and all the people had taken their places at the table. I attempted to behave as politely and refined as possible, because I desired Mrs. Chester Ross to view me as a well-mannered young girl despite my lack of beauty. Every detail proceeded smoothly until I observed Thirza approaching, carrying the plum pudding using one hand and the reheated pitcher of pudding sauce using the other. Isolde, I experienced a horrific moment. The entire situation rushed back to me, causing me to jump to my feet right at my seat and scream out, ‘Thirza, you mustn’t use that pudding sauce. There was a mouse drowned in it. I forgot to tell you before.’ Oh, Isolde, that horrifying instant will remain in my memory even if my life lasts a hundred years. Mrs. Chester Ross merely stared at me, making me feel as though I would drop through the floorboards from deep embarrassment. Being such an ideal homemaker, imagine the opinion she must have formed regarding our household. Thirza turned as red as a flame, though she remained completely silent—at that moment. She simply took that sauce and pudding back outside and returned with strawberry preserves instead. She even extended an offer of some to me, yet I was unable to get a single bite down. Receiving it felt like having hot coals poured onto my head. Once Mrs. Chester Ross departed, Thirza administered a severe reprimand to me. Why, Isolde, what is wrong?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0027 }

Isolde got up on her feet in a very shaky manner, after which she placed her hands on her head as she sat back down.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0028 }

“I’m—I’m terrible ill,” she spoke, somewhat slurringly. “I—I—have to return home immediately.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0029 }

“Oh, you cannot possibly think of returning home before having your tea,” Nell exclaimed, upset. “I will prepare it immediately—I will go make the tea this instant.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0030 }

“I am required to return to my home,” Isolde said once more, in a manner that was foolish yet resolute.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0031 }

“At least let me prepare a lunch for you,” Nell begged. “Allow me to offer you a slice of fruit cake along with a portion of the cherry preserves. Rest on the couch for a short time and your condition will improve. Exactly where does it hurt?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0032 }

“I have to return home,” Isolde stated, refusing to utter anything more. Nell begged her without success.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0033 }

“I have never known guests to leave prior to having tea,” she lamented. “Oh, Isolde, do you think there is any chance you are actually coming down with smallpox? Should that be the case, I will come to care for you, you may be certain of it. I will not abandon you ever. Even so, I really desire that you remain until tea is finished. In what part do you feel unwell?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0034 }

“My head is spinning terribly,” Isolde uttered.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0035 }

And she did, in truth, stagger as she went. Her eyes brimmed with disappointed tears as Nell retrieved the hat belonging to Isolde and accompanied her to the boundary fence of the Pembroke yard. Her weeping continued for the entire return journey to Grey Shutters; there, filled with sorrow, she returned the rest of the raspberry cordial to its spot in the pantry and set about preparing tea for Obed and Tobias, though any pleasure in doing so had vanished.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0036 }

It was Sunday on the following day, and Nell remained inside Grey Shutters the entire time because heavy rain fell continuously from morning until evening. Thirza dispatched her to Mrs. Sowerby’s to run a message on Monday afternoon. Nell returned rushing up the lane very quickly while tears streamed down her face. She burst into the kitchen and threw herself face down onto the sofa in extreme distress.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0037 }

“What is the problem this time, Nell?” asked Thirza, filled with doubt and dismay. “I certainly hope you have not been insolent to Mrs. Sowerby once more.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0038 }

Nell offered no reply, only weeping further and sobbing with greater force!
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0039 }

“Nell Harcourt, I expect an answer when I pose a question to you. Upright yourself this instant and explain to me the reason for your tears.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0040 }

Nell assumed an upright position, the very embodiment of tragedy.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0041 }

“Mrs. Sowerby visited Mrs. Pembroke today, and Mrs. Pembroke was extremely upset,” she cried out. “She claims that I got Isolde drunk on Saturday and delivered her home in a shameful state. Furthermore, she claims I must be a completely evil, bad little girl, and she vows she will never, ever allow Isolde to play with me again. Oh, Thirza, woe has simply overwhelmed me.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0042 }

Thirza gazed with complete astonishment.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0043 }

“Make Isolde intoxicated!” she uttered once she recovered her speech. “Nell, are you or Mrs. Pembroke out of your minds? What in the world did you administer to her?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0044 }

“There was nothing else besides raspberry cordial,” weeping, Nell wept. “Thirza, I never imagined that raspberry cordial could make anyone drunk—not even if three large glassfuls were consumed, which Isolde did. Oh, it seems so—so—much like the husband of Mrs. Thomas! However, making her drunk was never my intention.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0045 }

“Absolute nonsense about being drunk!” declared Thirza, stepping over to the pantry in the sitting room. Resting upon the shelf stood a bottle that she instantly identified as holding a portion of her three-year-old homemade currant wine, a beverage that had made her famous throughout Brierley, even if a few of the more rigid residents, including Mrs. Pembroke, voiced stern objections to it. Simultaneously, Thirza remembered that she had actually placed the bottle of raspberry cordial down in the cellar, rather than inside the pantry like she had informed Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0046 }

Holding the wine bottle, she returned to the kitchen. Unintentionally, her face twitched.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0047 }

“Nell, you truly possess a talent for causing mischief. You proceeded to offer Isolde currant wine rather than raspberry cordial. Were you not aware of the distinction yourself?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0048 }

“It never crossed my lips,” Nell stated. “My impression was that it was the cordial. My intention was to be so—so—welcoming. Isolde became terribly ill and was forced to return home. Mrs. Pembroke informed Mrs. Sowerby that she was merely dead drunk. When her mother inquired about what was wrong, she merely giggled in a foolish way and fell asleep, remaining asleep for hours. Upon smelling her breath, her mother recognized that she was drunk. Throughout the entire day yesterday, she suffered from a terrible headache. Mrs. Pembroke feels so outraged. Nothing will convince her otherwise than that I acted intentionally.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0049 }

“It seems to me that penalizing Isolde for such greediness in consuming three full glasses of any liquid would be more appropriate,” Thirza remarked curtly. “Indeed, three of those large goblets would have caused her illness even if the contents had merely been cordial. Anyhow, this incident will serve as a convenient argument for those individuals who criticize me so harshly regarding my currant wine production, despite the fact that I have abstained from making it for three years from the moment I learned of the minister's disapproval. That single bottle was preserved solely for medical needs. Come now, dear, dry your tears. I do not perceive how fault lies with you, even though I regret that this occurred.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0050 }

“I have to weep,” Nell declared. “My heart has been shattered. The stars in their paths do battle with me, Thirza. Isolde and I have been separated for all time. Oh, Thirza, I never imagined this outcome when we initially pledged our promises of devotion.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0051 }

“Stop being silly, Nell. As soon as Mrs. Pembroke realizes that you are not at fault, she will change her mind. She likely assumes you performed it as an unwise prank or something along those lines. It would be wise for you to go upstairs tonight and explain the situation to her.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0052 }

“The prospect of confronting the hurt mother of Isolde makes me lose my nerve,” Nell sighed. “I would prefer if you went instead, Thirza. Your composure far surpasses mine. She would probably be more inclined to hear you out than me.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0053 }

“Indeed, I shall,” Thirza replied, considering that taking such action would likely be prudent. “Stop weeping, Nell. Everything is going to be fine.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0054 }

Upon returning from Pear Hill, Thirza was no longer convinced that everything was all right. Spotting her approach, Nell rushed to the porch door in order to greet her.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0055 }

“Oh, Thirza, your expression tells me that it was all for nothing,” she remarked with sadness. “Will Mrs. Pembroke refuse to forgive me?”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0056 }

“Mrs. Pembroke indeed!” exclaimed Thirza sharply. “She is the most unreasonable woman I have ever encountered. Although I explained to her that it was entirely a mistake for which you were not responsible, she utterly refused to take my word. Furthermore, she made a point of bringing up my currant wine, reminding me how I had constantly claimed it was completely harmless to everyone. I simply informed her straight out that currant wine was never intended to be consumed three tumblers at a time, adding that if any child under my care proved to be that greedy, I would restore her sobriety with a thorough spanking.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0057 }

Thirza darted into the kitchen, severely agitated, leaving behind her in the porch a thoroughly bewildered little soul. Shortly afterward, Nell walked outside without a hat into the cold autumn twilight; with great resolve and an unhesitating step, she went down through the withered clover field across the log bridge and up through the spruce grove, illuminated by a faint small moon floating low above the western forest. Mrs. Pembroke, answering a faint knock at the door, discovered a white-lipped, bright-eyed petitioner standing on the threshold.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0058 }

Her expression grew stern. Possessing fierce animosities and biases, Mrs. Pembroke harbored a sullen, frigid type of rage that continuously proved the most difficult to conquer. Fairness demands acknowledging that she genuinely thought Nell had rendered Isolde intoxicated purely from premeditated ill intent, and she was sincerely eager to protect her young girl from the corruption of additional closeness with a child of that nature.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0059 }

“What is it that you want?” she asked in a rigid tone.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0060 }

Nell folded her hands together.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0061 }

“Oh, Mrs. Pembroke, I beg for your forgiveness. Intoxicating Isolde was never my intention—never. How could that be? Consider how it would feel if you happened to be a needy little orphan girl who was taken in by benevolent folks, with merely a single bosom friend in the whole world. Would you deliberately make her drunk, do you suppose? It seemed to me that it was nothing but raspberry cordial. I held the firm belief that it was raspberry cordial. Oh, I ask you not to say you intend to forbid Isolde from playing with me again. Should you do so, a black cloud of misery will hang over my existence.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0062 }

This statement, capable of melting kindly Mrs. Sowerby’s heart instantly, produced no impression upon Mrs. Pembroke other than to inflame her anger further. Distrusting the young girl's grand theatricality and elevated phrasing, she assumed Nell was mocking her. Consequently, she declared, with a cold cruelty:
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0063 }

“I do not consider you an appropriate young girl for Isolde to spend time with. You ought to return home and act properly.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0064 }

The lips of Nell trembled.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0065 }

“Will you not permit me a single final meeting with Isolde so I may bid her goodbye?” she begged.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0066 }

“Accompanied by her father, Isolde went to Delford,” remarked Mrs. Pembroke as she entered and closed the door.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0067 }

Nell returned to Grey Shutters, composed in her hopelessness.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0068 }

“I have no hope left,” she said to Thirza. “I visited Mrs. Pembroke in person, and her behavior toward me was extremely insulting. Thirza, she strikes me as a woman who lacks proper breeding. Nothing remains for us but prayer, though I doubt it will accomplish much, since, Thirza, it seems unlikely to me that even God can accomplish a great deal with someone as stubborn as Mrs. Pembroke.”
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0069 }

“Nell, you shouldn’t say such things” Thirza admonished, attempting to suppress that impious inclination to laugh which she was alarmed to feel increasing within herself. And in truth, upon recounting the entire tale to Obed that evening, she giggled openly about the hardships Nell endured.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0070 }

However, an unusual gentleness softened her features as she entered the east gable prior to retiring and discovered that Nell had wept until she fell asleep.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0071 }

“Poor little soul,” she whispered, raising an unfastened lock of hair away from the youth's wet-cheeked face. Afterwards, she leaned over and placed a kiss upon the reddened cheek resting on the pillow.
{: #nw-v01-c16-p0072 }
